title: Global Voices, Local Biases: Socio-Cultural Prejudices across Languages
findings: Statistically significant religious biases were found in models for Indian languages. In Hindi, DistilmBERT embeddings showed a significant association between religious terms and certain adjectives (effect size 0.965). In Bengali, a significant inverse association was found (effect size -1.179). The paper concludes that stereotypes prevalent in one language (e.g., bias against Muslims in Hindi) are not necessarily reflected equally in other related languages.

measurement_description: Measurement of stereotypical associations between religious terms and adjectives, specifically within the context of Indian languages. The paper cites an example of associating negative adjectives with the Muslim minority.
